6._: ABOUT, Sundial's as the base, reformed for the app (spine:pocket-beach 1.1111787197).
6.1: Most AI that people turn to for support is an open conversation with no shape and no end, its memory held inside someone else's product. This is the other kind: a daily practice, bounded, and the person's days are theirs.

2.1: This was made by Matthew Bushell, a therapeutic coach and Emotional Fitness practitioner with 5th Place, who lives with bipolar and serves on the Lived Experience Council of the International Society for Bipolar Disorders, with David Pinto, who created the beach it stands on, and with Claude; the companion is Gemma, an open model made by Google, running on your phone. It grew from lived experience, from Emotional Fitness, and from Presence in Action, Louie Gardiner's practice.

3.1: More and more people talk to AI about how they are. Those conversations are open-ended: no shape, no end, and a memory kept inside the company's product. They can turn a person in on themselves: more analysing, more self-watching, less living. This is made the other way, around a practice. Each day you say where you are; it gives your day back in your own words and turns you back to today. Done day after day, this can grow something. A clearer sense of what actually happened, what you felt, and the story you are telling about it. The steadiness to notice without being swept along. Over weeks, your days showing you where you tend to come to rest, and where you might step next. That is the hope in it: not to be fixed, but to be more present in your own life, and more free to choose. Nothing here can promise that; it is a practice, and the practice is yours. It is bounded: each day has a limit, and when it's reached, it rests until tomorrow. And your days are yours: a plain record under your name in an open system, not locked inside any one company, so you can read them, leave, or bring them to another AI.

4.1: Our days move with the light. Sundial keeps your practice in rhythm with it: the dial follows the real sun where you are, and there are no scores and no streaks, only the day's light and, over time, the hours you tend to come to it.

5.1: It reflects. It doesn't advise, interpret, diagnose or praise. Those are the instructions she is given here; they guide it but can't guarantee it, so you remain the judge of what's true for you. It isn't a friend or a therapist, and it won't pretend to be.

6.1: Everything you say and keep stays on this phone. The phone turns your voice into text itself, and Gemma, the companion, runs here too, so nothing you tell her is sent anywhere. Two things can leave, and only when you choose: a note you post to your room, sent when you tap Post; and, if you choose your own Claude as her voice, your words go to Anthropic each time she answers. Your days are kept in an open form, so you can save them, take them with you, and later, if you choose, bring them to the beach.

7.1: Emotional Fitness (5th Place) · The P6 Constellation and Presence in Action (Louie Gardiner) · Natural Inclusionality (Alan Rayner) · peer support and lived-experience recovery.
